title: Basic calculus of coherent functors and cones
statement:
Use the simplicial and enhanced notions of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], in the fixed size convention there. Let $K$ be any small simplicial set and $\mathscr C$ a quasicategory. Then $\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathscr C)$ and each of its full subcategories are quasicategories. Their mapping spaces, and the core of any quasicategory, are Kan complexes. A coherent transformation in $\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathscr C)$ is an equivalence if and only if all its vertex components are equivalences. Every functor equivalence induces equivalences on all mapping spaces.

For any coherent diagram $F:K\to\mathscr C$, the simplicial pullback defining the coherent cone category $(\Delta_K\downarrow F)$ is a quasicategory. For cones $\lambda:\Delta_Kx\to F$ and $\mu:\Delta_Ky\to F$, its mapping space from $\lambda$ to $\mu$ is naturally equivalent to the homotopy fiber over $\lambda$ of
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathscr C}(x,y)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathscr C)}(\Delta_Kx,F),\qquad a\longmapsto\mu\circ\Delta_K(a).$$
Consequently $\mu$ is limiting if and only if this displayed map is an equivalence for every $x$. The dual assertions hold for cocones and initial objects. In any quasicategory the full subcategory of terminal objects, if nonempty, is a contractible Kan complex; the same holds for initial objects. These statements concern arbitrary shapes and arbitrary diagrams, with no filteredness or invertibility assumption on their arrows.

proof.text: Apply [lem-cbc-internal-hom-quasicategory] with $A=K$, $X=\mathscr C$. A horn in a full subcategory fills in the ambient quasicategory; an inner horn contains every vertex of its simplex, so the filler has the prescribed vertices and belongs to the full subcategory. This proves functor-category and full-subcategory closure.

source.place: Lecture II, basic fact (1); full-subcategory closure from the definition.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison] to any quasicategory $Q$ and vertices $x,y$. Its statement directly gives that both the right-pinched mapping space $\operatorname{Map}_Q(x,y)$ and the edge mapping space $U_Q(x,y)$ are Kan complexes. Taking $Q$ to be the functor quasicategory or any full subcategory from step 1 proves the mapping-space assertion with exactly the mapping convention in the item.

source.place: Proposition 4.6.5.10, together with the Kan assertions stated in the existing pinch-comparison node.

proof.text: For the core of any quasicategory $Q$, fill an inner horn in $Q$, or an outer horn using [lem-cbc-equivalence-outer-horn-filling]. If $n>2$ the horn already contains every edge. If $n=2$, its new edge is a composite of the given equivalences or a composite with an inverse, and hence has an inverse by reversing these composites, using the triangle and associativity homotopies of [lem-cbc-simplicial-composition-spine]. Dimension-one horns fill by identities. Each filler therefore lies in the core, which is Kan.

source.place: Core closure, with its dimension-two edge check.

proof.text: Evaluation preserves inverse edges and triangle witnesses, so an equivalence transformation has equivalence components. Conversely assume the components of $\eta$ are equivalences. Any outer horn $\Lambda_0^n\to\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathscr C)$ with initial edge $\eta$ adjoints to $K\times\Lambda_0^n\to\mathscr C$. Apply [lem-cbc-invertible-prism-extension] with $A=\varnothing$, $B=K$. Its vertical-edge condition is exactly the component hypothesis. The extension adjoints to a filler. The converse implication of [lem-cbc-equivalence-outer-horn-filling], applied in this functor quasicategory, now makes $\eta$ an equivalence.

source.place: Prism extension with A empty, followed by the outer-horn criterion.

proof.text: Let $u:C\to D$ have quasi-inverse $v$ and natural equivalences $\alpha:vu\simeq\mathrm{id}_C$, $\beta:uv\simeq\mathrm{id}_D$. Define $T(f)=\alpha_Bv(f)\alpha_A^{-1}$ on mapping spaces. The multiarrow spaces and face maps of [lem-cbc-simplicial-composition-spine], together with the natural pinch comparison of [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison], supply composition maps and homotopies on the whole Kan spaces. A naturality square for $\alpha$ has edges $vu(a),a,\alpha_A,\alpha_B$; its two triangles identify $\alpha_Bvu(a)$ with $a\alpha_A$. Applying this square to every simplex of the mapping space gives $T(u(a))\simeq a$. Put $\delta_A=u(\alpha_A)\beta_{uA}^{-1}$ and $k(f)=\delta_B f\delta_A^{-1}$. The naturality squares for $\beta$ similarly give $u_*T\simeq k$. Composition with inverse edges gives a homotopy inverse $k^{-1}(f)=\delta_B^{-1}f\delta_A$. Since $Tu_*\simeq\mathrm{id}$, we have $ku_*\simeq u_*Tu_*\simeq u_*$ and hence $k^{-1}u_*\simeq u_*$. Consequently $R=T k^{-1}$ satisfies $u_*R\simeq\mathrm{id}$ and $Ru_*\simeq Tu_*\simeq\mathrm{id}$. Thus $u_*$ is a homotopy equivalence, and induces a bijection on components and isomorphisms on the based homotopy groups in the definition of weak equivalence. No triangle-compatible choices of the unit and counit were assumed.

source.place: Explicit conjugated quasi-inverse calculation using coherent composition.

proof.text: Put $D=\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathscr C)$ and $E_F=\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,D)\times_{\operatorname{ev}_1,D}\{F\}$. By [lem-coef-infinity-arrow-target-right-fibration], its source projection $q_F:E_F\to D$ is a right fibration. The exact degreewise pullback defining $P=(\Delta_K\downarrow F)$ is $\mathscr C\times_D E_F$. A horn lifting problem for $p:P\to\mathscr C$ therefore gives a horn lifting problem for $q_F$ over the simplex composed with $\Delta_K$; its lift pairs with that simplex to give the required lift in $P$. Thus $p$ is a right fibration. An inner horn in $P$ projects to one in $\mathscr C$; fill there and use this lifting property. Therefore $P$ is a quasicategory. Its fiber $P_x$ is exactly the edge mapping space $U_D(\Delta_Kx,F)$. The existing node [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison] says this is Kan and gives a natural homotopy equivalence from $\operatorname{Map}_D(\Delta_Kx,F)$ to it.

source.place: Proposition 4.6.4.13, pulled back along the constant-diagram functor by the explicit horn-lifting argument; pinch comparison is Proposition 4.6.5.10 (01L5).

proof.text: For $\mu\in P_y$, transport along $a:x\to y$ is $a^*\mu=\mu\circ\Delta_K(a)$: a lift is the square with upper edge $\Delta_K(a)$, lower edge the identity of $F$, and the composition triangle. The contractible composition-span fibers of [lem-cbc-simplicial-composition-spine] retain its higher compatibilities. Apply [lem-cbc-right-fibration-morphism-space]. It identifies $\operatorname{Map}_P(\lambda,\mu)$ with pairs $(a,\gamma)$, where $\gamma$ is a path from $\mu\Delta_K(a)$ to $\lambda$ in $P_x$. Using the natural pinch comparison of step 6 gives exactly the homotopy fiber in the item, with the path direction of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones].

source.place: Generic right-fibration mapping formula with explicit precomposition transport.

proof.text: Fix $\mu$, and denote the displayed map by $t_x$. Step 7 identifies its homotopy fiber over every target vertex $\lambda$ with $\operatorname{Map}_P(\lambda,\mu)$. By [lem-cbc-kan-fibration-fiber-criterion], $t_x$ is an equivalence exactly when all these fibers are contractible. As $x$ and $\lambda$ vary, they exhaust the objects of $P$. Thus this is terminality of $\mu$, the definition of a limiting cone. Empty target spaces cause no exception: existence of $t_x$ then forces its source empty as well.

Let $T$ be the full subcategory of terminal objects of a quasicategory $Q$, and suppose it has a vertex. By step 1 it is a quasicategory. For $n\geq1$, a boundary $\partial\Delta^n\to T$ has terminal last vertex. The criterion [lem-cbc-terminal-boundary-extension] fills it in $Q$; its vertices are the boundary vertices, so fullness places it in $T$. For $n=0$ choose the given vertex. Hence $T\to\Delta^0$ lifts every boundary. To fill a horn, first fill its missing face from that face's boundary (when $n=1$, choose its missing vertex), then fill the whole boundary. Thus $T$ is Kan. Now [lem-cbc-kan-fibration-fiber-criterion] makes $T\to\Delta^0$ a weak equivalence, proving contractibility of the full subcategory itself. With no terminal vertices it and its core are empty.

source.place: Boundary criterion followed by the trivial Kan fibration criterion.

proof.text: Replace $\mathscr C$ by its opposite, reversing simplex vertex order. This sends $\Lambda_i^n$ to $\Lambda_{n-i}^n$, so preserves quasicategories and exchanges terminal with initial. A cone $\Delta_{K^{\mathrm{op}}}x\to F^{\mathrm{op}}$ becomes a cocone $F\to\Delta_Kx$, reversing cone-category arrows. Do not identify the opposite of a right-pinched simplicial set with a right-pinched simplicial set strictly. Instead apply [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison] separately in $\mathscr C$ and $\mathscr C^{\mathrm{op}}$. Reversing the arrow interval identifies $U_{\mathscr C^{\mathrm{op}}}(x,y)$ with $U_{\mathscr C}(y,x)^{\mathrm{op}}$. For any simplicial set $S$, the coordinate reversal $(s;t_0,\ldots,t_n)\mapsto(s;t_n,\ldots,t_0)$ gives a homeomorphism $|S^{\mathrm{op}}|\cong|S|$: the realization relations agree because the opposite operator sends a monotone map $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$ to $i\mapsto n-\alpha(m-i)$. Hence these comparisons identify the two mapping-space homotopy types and preserve contractibility. Steps 6-8 therefore give the cocone mapping formula and the criterion that $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathscr C}(y,x)\to\operatorname{Map}_D(F,\Delta_Kx)$ be an equivalence for a cocone $F\to\Delta_Ky$. Step 9 in the opposite proves contractibility for the initial-object full subcategory. No argument used filteredness, nonempty $K$, or invertibility of diagram arrows.
